judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital states the license is granted "solely for the purposes of" operating Hotel/Casinos and selling merchandise "in the Hotel/Casinos or Casinos", a purpose limitation whose reach is uncertain on its own terms. "Solely" invites an argument that the whole grant is narrower than the operative language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital's confinement of merchandise sales to inside the Hotel/Casinos in the Morton Territories sits against operative clause 2(b)(v), which lets Licensee sell Licensed Products over the Internet, and against 2(a), which allows worldwide promotion — a classic recital-versus-operative divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All confusingly similar names, marks and logos ... and derivations thereof, to the maximum extent permitted by law" is an open-ended catch-all following a short enumerated list, with no ascertainable boundary. The exclusion of the Hotel/Casino Marks then has to be reconciled with that sweep.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 2(b)(iii) (no use of any Hard Rock Marks not expressly provided) and 6(c) (Licensee may nonetheless use the "Hard Rock" designation for locations and areas), which pull in different directions about a term inside this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is by reference to Exhibit A and is largely mechanical, though the trailing "except as expressly provided herein" leaves the exclusion of other Hard Rock Marks porous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A lists both "Hard Rock Casino" and "Hard Rock Hotel", so it overlaps entirely with Exhibit B (1(c)), making the Hotel/Casino Marks split hard to maintain against 2(b)(i) and 3(a), which turn on that distinction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition by reference to an exhibit; the only soft edge is "except as expressly provided herein".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B ("Hard Rock Casino") duplicates part of Exhibit A, so the Casino Marks and Hotel Marks are not cleanly separable, which matters for 3(a)'s allocation of worldwide hotel-only rights to Licensor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All-inclusive place for lodging, with indoor corridors and offering a variety of amenities" is vague at the edges — "all-inclusive" and "a variety of amenities" have no measurable boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term drives 2(b)(i) and the Nevada carve-out in 3(a), so a borderline lodging facility could be argued either way, but nothing in the instrument contradicts the definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Substantial source of revenue and its principal function" is a vague dual test, and "such as slot machines, gaming tables and the like" is an ejusdem generis catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The riverboat sentence dovetails with 2(b)(ix) rather than conflicting with it, and no other provision cuts against this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Immediately adjoining contiguous facility" and "part of the same 'Hard Rock' complex/development" are undefined spatial concepts that two parties could reasonably apply differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds 2(b)(i) and 2(b)(iv) ("in or contiguous to"), which use similar loose language, but I found no direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short derivative definition confined to the Morton Territories; nothing in the words themselves is ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3(a) prohibits Licensor from owning a "Hard Rock Hotel" in Nevada even though the defined term is limited to Licensee's territories, and 2(b)(vii) speaks of "other Hard Rock Hotels" although 2(b)(i) bars Licensee from using the Hotel Marks in a hotel that is not a Hotel/Casino.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward derivative definition with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2(b)(i) and 1(e); no competing provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple derivative definition; "and/or" is the only softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 2(a) and 2(b)(i); nothing elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A collective definition; no ambiguous term to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2(b)(vii) refers to "any other Hard Rock Facility developed, operated, owned, or managed by Licensee" although Licensee is barred from operating Hard Rock Cafe restaurants (2(b)(ii)), a small definitional mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains obvious mechanical slips ("fifty (SO) mile radius form the City Hall") and a self-referential geographic test ("City Hall or other similarly recognized civic center structure located reasonably near the geographic center"), plus a nested exception-to-an-exception for Texas/Houston.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The territory is the pivot of 2(a), 3(a) and 8(a)(1); Illinois is expressly included although east of the Mississippi, which is a drafted inclusion rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any and all services provided by Licensee in connection with or relating to the operation of" is an extremely broad and boundaryless formula, and the text is garbled ("Hard Rock Hotei/Casinos"). Whether ancillary services (restaurants, retail, online offerings) fall inside is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term carries the quality obligations in 4(a)-(e) and the marking obligation in 4(e), and interacts with 2(a)'s territorial confinement and 2(b)(ii)'s restaurant carve-out, so its breadth can be argued to sweep in activities other clauses treat as outside the licence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any and all personal property, products and merchandise bearing the ... Marks and offered for sale or sold by Licensee" is broad but reasonably self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs 2(b)(iv)-(v), where the geographic-location marking rule and the Internet carve-out create the real friction rather than this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple identification of the party, extended to successors, assigns and transferees.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12 gives the Licensor notice address as "Hard Rock Cafe International (DEL), Inc." rather than Rank Licensing, and 3(a) speaks of "any affiliated entity", so who counts as Licensor for particular obligations is not perfectly aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is "exclusive" yet "only in the Morton Territories" and "solely in connection with" listed activities, and the worldwide promotion carve-out excepts "the sale of merchandise" — the boundary between permitted promotion/advertising and prohibited exploitation outside the territory is genuinely contestable. The warranty is also qualified by an opaque proviso about "whatever actions or inactions may have been taken or not taken by Morton".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with 3(a), which lets Licensor exploit the Hotel Marks "anywhere in the world" for a hotel without a casino, and with 2(b)(v), which permits Internet sales that are inherently extraterritorial — both cut against the exclusivity and the territorial bar stated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two clear, complementary sentences keyed to defined terms; little to construe internally.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with 3(a) (Licensor may use the Hotel Marks worldwide for a hotel without a casino) and with 2(b)(vii)'s reference to "other Hard Rock Hotels", which sits awkwardly with the prohibition here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The modifier is misplaced: "any restaurant in any Hard Rock Hotel/Casino ... or anywhere else that is confusingly similar" can be read as barring all restaurants inside the facilities, or only confusingly similar ones. The second sentence's saving language shows the tension rather than curing it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against 1(j) and 8(a) (Hard Rock Cafe restaurants belong to Licensor) the intent is discernible, and I found no direct contradiction elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Sole right to apply" is immediately qualified by a mandatory consent sentence and a "best efforts" maintenance duty triggered by a failure "reasonably likely to affect" the marks — vague and internally tangled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The agency fallback here is the express exception carved out in Section 13's no-agency clause, and it also cuts against 6(b)'s blanket prohibition on Licensee filings, so the provisions must be harmonised carefully.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Stand alone merchandise outlet", "contiguous to" and "must always bear the geographic location where sold" are all elastic phrases, and the Licensor-side restriction is drafted with a compound "where there is both a Hard Rock Hotel/Casino or Hard Rock Casino and a Hard Rock Cafe restaurant" whose condition is ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly yields to 2(b)(v) (Internet sales) and 2(b)(vii), and its geographic-marking rule sits against 2(b)(vi)'s logo requirements, so its scope depends on how those carve-outs are read.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Licensed Products that bear the Internet address as the Licensed Products' location" and the exception for "Hard Rock Internet access kits" are odd, undefined formulations with an unclear separation of merchandise lines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Internet sales are inherently worldwide, which is difficult to square with 2(a)'s bar on exploiting the Marks outside the Morton Territories and with the recital confining merchandise sales to the Hotel/Casinos; 8(b) also allocates web activity by territory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Other designations such as 'Beach Club' or 'Athletic Club'" is an open list after a specific prescription, and Exhibit C is a fragmentary reproduction, so the permitted logo forms are not fully fixed by the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The designations it permits inside the facilities are the same ones treated in 2(b)(vii) and 2(b)(viii) and in 3(d), which bars any qualifier "other than geographical designations" — those provisions do not obviously agree.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Currently in use ... as of the date of this Agreement" and the split between using a designation and selling merchandise bearing it are workable, but the eighteen-month proviso is drafted awkwardly against the general permission.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D and Exhibit E list the identical designations ("Beach Club"/"Athletic Club"), yet 2(b)(vii) permits continuing use in other facilities while 2(b)(viii) requires the Licensee to "forever cease displaying such designations" after eighteen months — a genuine internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Whatever merchandise is currently being sold" is imprecise, and "forever cease displaying such designations" is absolute in a way the preceding subclause is not.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Exhibit E duplicates Exhibit D, this permanent cessation contradicts 2(b)(vii)'s ongoing permission to use the same designations, and both sit against 2(b)(vi).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contingent, narrowly drawn permission keyed to a legal requirement; "such as" appears twice but the operative trigger is objective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly routes back to 2(b)(iii) and matches the riverboat sentence in 1(e), so it fits the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The long third sentence bundles a reservation, a worldwide right to exploit the Hotel Marks "for a Hotel facility that does not include a Casino", and a Nevada exception, leaving the geographic reach of Licensor's hotel rights inside the Morton Territories genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the clause 2(a) is expressly made subject to, and it appears to permit Licensor to use the Hotel Marks in the Morton Territories for casino-free hotels notwithstanding the "exclusive" licence in 2(a); Section 11(a) then singles out only the Nevada prohibition for injunctive protection.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Never to attack or assist another in attacking" is broad but its subject matter is specified; the phrase "during the Term of this Agreement or thereafter" is odd in a perpetual licence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits uneasily with 5(d), which expressly contemplates that disputes about "the validity of this License Agreement or the validity or enforceability of any trademark rights" will be litigated in court, and with 9(a)'s perpetual term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard goodwill-inurement acknowledgment with no contestable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3(a) and 3(b); no competing provision located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Dominate, modify or qualify" is vague, and the carve-out "other than geographical designations" is narrow relative to what the Agreement elsewhere allows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2(b)(vi) expressly permits replacing the geographic wording with "Beach Club" or "Athletic Club", which are not geographical designations — a direct tension with this prohibition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short catch-all covenant tied to the rest of the Agreement; nothing ambiguous to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply restates the structure of Section 2 and 3; no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The quality benchmark is doubly vague: "good quality at least as high as the quality of similar goods presently sold" at the Las Vegas property, and additional items must be "equal to and commensurate with" existing ones, with no measurable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This standard is the trigger for the cure-and-arbitrate machinery in 5(a) ("any substantial failure ... to maintain in any respect quality standards") and is characterised in 4(f) as existing solely to protect goodwill, so its content controls whether a dispute is arbitrable at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonable access", "reasonable notice" and "without disruption" are conventional reasonableness qualifiers rather than genuine ambiguities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits with 4(c), 4(f) and Section 13's explanation of the supervision rights; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is syntactically garbled — "furnish or render ... requested Licensed Services, representative samples on the premises of each Licensed Product" — so what exactly must be produced is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the inspection right in 4(b) and works with it; nothing elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, standard compliance covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision in the instrument pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Wherever the same may be used with reasonable convenience" and "the appropriate notice of registration" are both indeterminate obligations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 2(b)(vi)'s prescribed logo form and 2(a)'s worldwide promotion permission, but there is no outright conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A purposive acknowledgment; "solely to ensure the quality" is definite in direction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the theme of Section 13 and is consistent with 4(b)-(c); no inconsistency located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arbitration trigger — "any dispute regarding the failure of Licensee to conform to any provision of quality control as set forth herein" — has an uncertain perimeter, and the clause mixes an undefined "substantial failure" threshold with a rigid thirty-day cure; "proscribed" for "prescribed" is a mechanical error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its scope has to be squared with 5(d), which excludes everything "not specifically identified hereinabove" from arbitration, and with Section 14, which sends all other claims to New York courts while this clause alternates the forum between California and New York.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but plainly worded grant of remedial power to the arbitrators.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The arbitrators' injunctive power overlaps with Section 11(a)'s promise of court-ordered injunctions and 5(d)'s court carve-out, creating some allocation friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite timing and finality language; the thirty-business-day deadline is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Enforcement under New York law matches Section 14's choice of law; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any claims or controversies not specifically identified hereinabove, including but not limited to" is exactly the general-versus-specific structure that leaves the carve-out's reach uncertain, and it defines the arbitral scope only by negative implication from 5(a).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with 5(a)'s arbitration mandate and with Section 14's forum clause, and it contemplates court litigation of validity questions that 3(b) forbids Licensee from raising at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line mutual "best efforts to protect the Marks" covenant with no specified content — the standard of performance and what "protect" requires are both indeterminate. Its brevity is precisely what makes it contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read against 2(b)(iii) (Licensor's sole registration right and its own best-efforts maintenance duty) and 6(d) (each party may sue at its own cost, with Licensor controlling joint proceedings), which allocate protection duties in more specific and not obviously consistent ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Affect the ownership of or encumber, damage, dilute or modify" is broad, but the prohibition is clear in direction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 2(b)(iii)'s fallback allowing Licensee to prepare and file registration documents as Licensor's agent, which is an express exception this clause does not acknowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence "only as expressly provided herein in clause 2(b), Licensee may use the 'Hard Rock' designation ... but shall not use, sell or display any merchandise bearing such designations" is awkwardly constructed and its merchandise bar is hard to delimit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2(b)(vii) expressly allowed merchandise bearing certain designations to be sold for eighteen months, and 2(b)(iv)-(v) permit sale of Licensed Products generally, so this blanket merchandise prohibition does not sit comfortably with Section 2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause first says each party sues at its own cost with recoveries "for the account of such party", then says Licensor "will always have full control of any joint proceedings" with costs and recoveries shared equally, without defining when a proceeding becomes "joint".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The control and cost-sharing regime here overlaps with Section 11(a)'s remedies clause and with 6(a)'s mutual best-efforts duty, and the last sentence's denial of authority to act in Licensor's name sits against 2(b)(iii)'s agency fallback.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sided indemnity covering anything "in relation to the Hard Rock Hotel Marks, or the Hard Rock Casino Marks or either of them" — a sweep broad enough to capture losses arising from Licensor's own conduct, and any genuine ambiguity would be construed against its drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is no reciprocal indemnity anywhere, and it must coexist with 2(a)'s ownership warranty by Licensor and 6(d)'s each-party-bears-its-own-costs litigation regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "When practical and appropriate" makes the core cooperation duty essentially unmeasurable, and the table-display obligation is oddly made "reasonably acceptable to Licensor" — apparently a slip for Licensee, since it is Licensor's own display promoting Licensee's facilities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The quarterly/one-week display duty binds Licensor in the Morton Territories only and sits with 8(a)(3) and 8(b), but the qualifier makes it hard to say what Section 8's cooperation scheme actually requires of either side.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific, factual attribution obligation triggered by a defined event; little to construe beyond "sponsored by".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the instrument addresses attribution, so no conflict arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Same size and style" is a modest standard and the trigger ("any map ... which identifies all locations") is reasonably concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1(j) and the rest of Section 8; no competing provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Agree to discuss the possibility" is an agreement to agree with no ascertainable obligation, which is the sort of language parties do fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds nothing that contradicts the rest of Section 8 or the grant clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Licensor may develop ... except that Licensee may develop ... a Web page for the Hard Rock Hotel/Casinos or Casinos in the Morton Territories" leaves it unclear whether Licensee's web right is exclusive as to those properties and what "in the Morton Territories" modifies for a medium with no location.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with 2(a)'s bar on exploiting the Marks outside the Morton Territories and with 2(b)(v)'s Internet sales carve-out, which together make the territorial allocation of an inherently global medium genuinely incoherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "A license granted in perpetuity" is definite on its face; the heading promises "options" the clause never supplies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16 assumes the Agreement can be terminated and 5(a) provides a cure regime, yet there is no termination provision anywhere — a whole-instrument mismatch with this perpetual term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Royalty-free and fully paid is unambiguous; "solely entitled to all economic benefits" is broad but directional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 6(d)'s equal division of recoveries in joint proceedings and 9(c)'s first-offer right, but neither squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All or substantially all of his assets and/or rights in connection with the use and exploitation" of the Marks is an imprecise trigger, and the good-faith negotiation duty with a thirty-day and six-month timetable is only loosely specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10 lets Licensee sublicense or franchise "any or all of the rights" without any first-offer step, and Section 18 makes the Agreement binding on transferees and assigns, so the first-offer right can be argued to be circumventable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any or all of the rights and licenses granted hereunder" with no consent requirement is a sweeping right, and the flow-down obligation ("assume, observe and perform all of the obligations of Licensee") is stated without limit or remedy for non-compliance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An unrestricted right to sublicense all rights can be read to let Licensee transfer everything without triggering the 9(c) first-offer negotiation, and it sits against 2(a)'s "solely in connection with" limits, 3(a)'s reservation and Section 7's indemnity for sublicensees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully drafted; the acknowledgment that money damages are inadequate and the remedies-are-cumulative sentence are conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It promises court injunctions while 5(a)-(b) send quality disputes to arbitrators expressly empowered to grant injunctions, and it singles out only the Nevada prohibition for Licensee's benefit though 3(a) contains other Licensor restrictions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard anti-waiver language, mutual and clearly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 22 requires waivers to be in signed writing, which reinforces rather than contradicts this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The delivery methods and deemed-receipt rules are specified for each channel; no ambiguous term stands out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Licensor notice party is "Hard Rock Cafe International (DEL), Inc.", not Rank Licensing, Inc. as defined in 1(n), an unexplained mismatch with the definition and the signature block.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Nor be deemed to be coupled with an interest" and the blanket denial of any granted power are broad, but the clause is internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly excepts 2(b)(iii)'s agency mechanism, which shows the drafters harmonised the two; 6(d)'s last sentence points the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement" is broad but standard, and the Section 5 carve-out is signposted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5(a) sets an arbitral forum alternating between California and New York while this clause fixes New York courts, and 5(d)'s residual carve-out determines which claims land where — the interlock is not clean.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate severability, plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision in the instrument cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Which, in order to be effective, or by its nature, must survive" is a self-referential and imprecise test for which terms survive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a termination that 9(a) — a perpetual licence with no termination mechanism anywhere in the Agreement — never provides for.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to "the Purchase and Sale Agreement" without defining or identifying it, and then extinguishes rights under named prior settlement agreements "including but not limited to" certain documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The merger is limited "with respect to the licensing of the Hard Rock Hotel Marks and Hard Rock Casino Marks", so how it interacts with the unnamed Purchase and Sale Agreement and the extinguished 1985/1995 settlements, and with Section 23's amendment rule, is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional successors-and-assigns language; the reference to heirs and executors fits an individual Licensee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It benefits "transferees, and assigns" without qualification although 9(c) conditions Licensee's transfers on a first-offer negotiation and 1(n) contemplates Licensor's successors — a mild tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, standard authority representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2(a) contains a qualified ownership warranty and there is no corresponding Licensee authority clause, but nothing contradicts this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard enforceability representation with the usual equitable and insolvency qualifications.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to "all of the Parties" in a two-party agreement, a trivial slip with no operative consequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause uses "the Morton Parties" and "the Rank Parties", capitalised terms that are defined nowhere in this Agreement, leaving the scope of the representation genuinely uncertain. The list "contract, agreement, indenture, lease, promissory note, license or other commitment" also ends in an unbounded catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The only defined parties are Licensor (1(n)) and Licensee, so the imported terminology suggests the clause was lifted from the related Purchase and Sale Agreement referenced in Section 17 and does not fit this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear formality requirement for waivers; "the party or parties entitled to the benefit thereof" is determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces 11(b)'s anti-waiver clause and Section 23; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The inclusion of "or interpreted" among the things that may be done "only by written instrument" is unusual and arguably nonsensical, since interpretation is a judicial function.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the no-oral-modification sentence in Section 17 without contradicting it.
